findings: Specific-module register_forward_pre_hook can replace declared module inputs and register_forward_hook can replace outputs.
Both use RemovableHandle, allowing explicit teardown and a post-removal equivalence test.
PyTorch skips the hook path when no hooks exist, supporting a low-persistent-overhead experiment shape.
Global hooks are the wrong integration shape because they introduce global state; use exact specific-module hooks only.
Historical PyTorch compile/hook issues mean exact target runtime/build compatibility must be tested; eager mode is the safer first falsifier.
Native hooks provide tensor intervention only and cannot replace WP507 GWT recipient receipts, canonical truth/state, effect authority or checkpoint-consumption evidence.
hypothesis: If the exact local approximately-0.8B target already executes through a compatible PyTorch eager module path, a thin F2-owned native-hook adapter should be the lowest-resource first mechanism for lesion/rescue testing of model-internal GWT/J-Space influence, and should be compared against TransformerLens/pyvene only after an exact-model E3 reversibility/equivalence falsifier.
counterhypothesis: A compiled/fused/non-PyTorch target may make Python module hooks incomplete or semantically perturbing, in which case a dedicated intervention framework or lower-level runtime hook is preferable despite higher dependency cost.
next_gate: Acquire a new E3 claim only when exact checkpoint/tokenizer/runtime/build identity exists; run baseline -> no-op hook -> one predeclared lesion/rescue -> remove hook -> post-removal baseline, binding module path, intervention digest and raw output receipt. No E5 candidate from E2 alone.
